user_intent: Document even-power nonnegativity, carefully guarded power monotonicity and familiar inequalities such as a^2+b^2>=2ab in the mathematics lookup.

new_sections: R15 power signs and two kinds of monotonicity
R16 common real inequalities at a glance
publication.late_power_table: Mathematical directions now distinguish themselves from certified proof coverage.

mathematical_contracts.even_natural: Real x, natural n: x^(2*n)=(x^n)^2>=0, including zero base and n=0 under 0^0=1.
mathematical_contracts.even_integer_strict: Nonzero real x, integer n: expose x^n!=0 then x^(2*n)=(x^n)^2>0. Includes negative exponents.
mathematical_contracts.odd_negative: Real x<0, natural n: explicit nonzero bridge and even-part factorization give x^(2*n+1)<0.
mathematical_contracts.base_order: Nonnegative ordered bases and a positive natural exponent give a^n<=b^n. Even powers do not preserve signed order on the whole real line.
mathematical_contracts.exponent_order: Positive base >=1 and integer m<=n give weak growth; >1 and m<n give strict growth. Base=1 is constant. A positive base <=1 gives integer-exponent decay.
mathematical_contracts.range_bounds: For a>=1 and positive natural n, a<=a^n. For a in [0,1] and positive natural n, 0<=a^n<=a.
mathematical_contracts.real_exponents: Positive-base real powers have checked WD/positivity; general real-exponent order is a true mathematical law but not certified by the accepted integer-order packages here.

proof_derivation: Integer exponent growth -> natural power >=1 by induction -> nonnegative exponent gap -> multiplication by positive power
Integer exponent decay -> natural power <=1 by induction -> the same nonnegative gap -> positive multiplication
Strict growth -> positive gap -> power bounded below by base >1
Common estimates -> existing square/product proof owners, preserving each domain
